intro: Most people in Poland are Polish and Catholic, and family traditions run deep. Millions of Poles also live abroad, and since 2022 Poland has become home to many Ukrainians.

chapters.title: Cities
text: Warsaw, the capital, was rebuilt after the war and is now a modern business centre. Kraków, the old royal capital, survived the war almost undamaged, and Łódź, Wrocław, Poznań and Gdańsk are other big cities.

chapters.title: Language and faith
text: Polish is a West Slavic language written in the Latin alphabet with extra letters such as ą, ę, ł and ż, and is famous for tongue-twisters full of consonants. Most Poles are Roman Catholic, and the church played a big role in resisting communism.
Millions of people of Polish origin live in the United States, Germany and the UK. Since 2022, more than a million Ukrainians have settled in Poland.

chapters.title: Family traditions
text: Many Poles celebrate their name day, the feast of the saint they are named after, as much as their birthday. On Christmas Eve families share a meatless supper of twelve dishes and leave an empty place at the table for an unexpected guest. On Easter Monday, people soak each other with water.

keyTerms.meaning: A celebration on the feast day of the saint who shares your name.
A family of languages including Polish, Russian, Czech and Ukrainian.
